f(2) = −8 + 16 − 3 = 5, so the maximum is 5, not −3.
Answer: D.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: The simplified form of ((6x − 12)/(6x)) × (8x²/(x − 2)), where x ≠ 0, 2, is equal to:
explanation_steps: 6x − 12 = 6(x − 2), so the first fraction is (x − 2)/x.
Answer: A.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: If log x = s and log y = t, then the value of log((x⁴ y⁻⁴)/(xy)²) is:
explanation_steps: The argument is x⁴ y⁻⁴ / (x² y²) = x² y⁻⁶.
log(x² / y⁶) = 2s − 6t. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: Which of the following functions has a graph symmetrical with respect to the y-axis?
explanation_steps: Symmetry about the y-axis means the function is even: f(−x) = f(x).
Only 1/(x² − 1) is even. The others change sign or are neither even nor odd.
Answer: B.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: If f(x) = −x² + x + 4, then f(−x) is equal to:
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: The length of a small fish in Assab coastal waters (in millimetres) is approximated by f(x) = 30x/(x + 2), where x is measured in weeks. Which of the following is true?
options: The length of the fish would be 10 mm after three weeks.
The length will never reach 30 mm in the fish’s lifetime.
The length of the fish would be 24 mm after four weeks.
The length of the fish would be 52 mm after a year.
explanation_steps: f(3) = 18, f(4) = 20, and f(52) ≈ 28.9, so A, C and D are false.
30x/(x + 2) = 30 − 60/(x + 2) is always less than 30 for finite x > 0.
Answer: B.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: The height in metres of a rocket fired upward from the ground with an initial velocity of 1600 m/s is H(t) = −16t² + 1600t. The maximum height which the rocket can reach is
explanation_steps: The vertex is at t = 1600/(32) = 50 s.
Answer: B.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: The inverse of the exponential function y = 3^(2x − 4) is:
explanation_steps: log₃ y = 2x − 4, so x = 2 + (1/2) log₃ y.
Interchange variables: y = 2 + log₃(√x).
Answer: C.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: Suppose α and β are roots of 2x² + px − 8 = 0. If α + β = 4, then the value of p is:
explanation_steps: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a.
−p/2 = 4, so p = −8. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: The solution set of (2x + 4)/(x − 2) = 2 is:
options: The set of all real numbers.
The set of all real numbers except 2.
explanation_steps: 2x + 4 = 2(x − 2) gives 4 = −4, a contradiction.
x = 2 is also excluded. The solution set is empty. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Algebra and Geometry
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements could be represented by a linear function?
options: The length of a diagonal of a square is equal to its side times √2.
The surface area of a sphere is equal to 4π times the square of the radius.
The cost of drilling a water well is equal to 4 times the cube of the depth.
The kinetic energy of a moving body is equal to half of its mass times the square of the velocity.
explanation_steps: Diagonal = (√2) × side is linear in the side.
B, C and D are quadratic or cubic. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The two main branches of physical sciences are
explanation_steps: The physical sciences are physics and chemistry. Biology is a life science. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An airplane takes off at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. If the horizontal component of its velocity is 200 m/s, then the vertical component of its velocity and resultant speed in m/s are, respectively. (Take cos 45° = sin 45° = 0.707.)
explanation_steps: At 45°, vx = v cos 45° and vy = v sin 45°, so vy = vx = 200 m/s.
Resultant speed v = 200 / 0.707 = 282.9 m/s, matching 282.8. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If an object starting from rest is moving with acceleration of 15 cm/s², then the distance in meters traveled by it in 10 s is
explanation_steps: 15 cm/s² = 0.15 m/s². From rest, s = ½at² = ½ × 0.15 × 100 = 7.5 m. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A body moving at 40 m/s stops in 5 s. The body's deceleration in m/s² (assumed to be constant) and the distance in meters traveled by it are, respectively,

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: In projectile motion, at the peak of the trajectory, both the vertical and horizontal components of velocity are zero.
If an object is moving in uniform circular motion, it is accelerating.
As the radius of the circular path increases, the centripetal acceleration decreases, provided that the velocity remains the same.
In the motion of the moon around the earth, the force that provides the necessary centripetal acceleration is the gravitational attraction of the earth.
In a projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity is always constant if air resistance is neglected.
explanation_steps: At the peak, only the vertical component is zero. The horizontal component stays constant if air resistance is neglected.
B–E are correct. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: One of the following statements is not correct.
options: A single force acting on a body can produce rotational motion.
A single force acting on a body can produce translational motion.
The moment of a force can be zero when a single force acts on a body.
The effect of a force in producing rotation depends only on the force itself.
The center of gravity of a homogeneous sphere lies at its geometric center.
explanation_steps: The turning effect also depends on the perpendicular distance from the pivot (the moment arm).
A force through the centre gives zero moment, so C is possible. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the wrong statement from the following.
options: The area under the force-displacement curve is equal to the work done by the force.
Potential energy is a function of position.
The kinetic energy of a body depends on the frame of reference.
During elastic collisions only the total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant.
The resultant work done on a particle is equal to the resulting change in its translational kinetic energy.
explanation_steps: In an elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy of an isolated system stay constant.
Saying only momentum remains constant is wrong. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: From the following, choose the statement which is not true.
options: The ratio of the load to effort is called actual mechanical advantage.
Ideal mechanical advantage is always less than actual mechanical advantage.
Actual mechanical advantage of machines can be greater than 1, or less than 1.
Simple machines have friction in their moving parts; thus the effort applied must overcome both the force of friction and the load.
The greater the frictional force in a machine, the smaller is its actual mechanical advantage.
explanation_steps: Friction makes actual mechanical advantage less than or equal to the ideal value, not greater.
Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is not true?
options: In practical applications we always get less work out of a machine than we put in.
It can be said that a machine is any device used to change the magnitude or direction of a force.
A single fixed pulley is a direction changer and not a force multiplier.
If 250 J is the useful work output of a machine for a 450 J input work, the efficiency is 1.8 or 180%.
The work output is the work done by the machine.
explanation_steps: Efficiency = useful output / input = 250/450 = 0.556, or 55.6%, not 180%.
The printed claim is the false statement. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: All the following statements are true except one. Choose the one which is not true.
options: The SI unit of surface tension is N/m or J/m².
The phenomenon by which the surface of a liquid is elevated or depressed where it is in contact with a solid is called capillarity.
Some insects can walk on the surface of water because they are kept afloat by surface tension.
Surface tension causes suspended droplets, for example rain drops, to acquire a spherical shape.
A steel needle floats when it is entirely on the surface of water due to Archimedes' principle.
explanation_steps: A needle denser than water is supported by surface tension, not by buoyancy.
A–D are true. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The statements below are about the expansion of a liquid in a container when it is heated. Choose the statement which is not correct.
options: The expansion observed under such a condition is the apparent expansion of the liquid.
The true expansion of the liquid is less than the apparent expansion.
The true expansion of the liquid is greater than the apparent expansion.
Under such conditions both the liquid and the containing vessel expand.
The apparent expansion of the liquid observed is less than the real or true expansion of the liquid.
explanation_steps: The vessel also expands, so the observed (apparent) expansion is less than the true expansion.
B reverses that relation. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Most substances expand when heated and contract when cooled; but one of the following substances is an exception to this rule. Which one is it?
explanation_steps: Water contracts when warmed from 0 °C to 4 °C. The metals and mercury expand on heating. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following comparisons among static friction, sliding friction and rolling friction is the most appropriate? Static friction is
options: less than sliding friction and sliding friction is greater than rolling friction.
greater than sliding friction and sliding friction is less than rolling friction.
greater than sliding friction and sliding friction is greater than rolling friction.
less than sliding friction and sliding friction is less than rolling friction.
greater than sliding friction and rolling friction is greater than sliding friction.
explanation_steps: For the same surfaces, limiting static friction is greater than kinetic (sliding) friction, and sliding friction is greater than rolling friction. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose from the following factors the one that does not increase the rate of evaporation of a liquid.
options: Increasing the temperature of the liquid.
Reducing the air pressure above the liquid.
Increasing the surface of the liquid.
Causing a draught so as to remove the vapor molecules before they have a chance to return to the liquid.
Increasing the air pressure above the liquid.
explanation_steps: Higher pressure above the liquid slows evaporation. A–D all increase the rate. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: All the following statements are correct except one. Choose the one which is not correct.
options: In a simple harmonic oscillation, the amplitude A is constant.
The period T of a simple harmonic motion is dependent on the amplitude.
The energy of any simple harmonic oscillator is proportional to the square of the amplitude.
Simple harmonic motion is a motion that occurs without loss of energy.
If friction is present in an oscillatory motion, the oscillation is not simple harmonic.
explanation_steps: For SHM the period does not depend on amplitude.
Energy is proportional to A², and ideal SHM has no energy loss. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If the frequency of a simple pendulum is 0.6 Hz, then the length of the pendulum in meter is. (Take g = 10 m/s².)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The frequency in hertz of a wave whose wavelength is 2.0 m and speed 340 m/s is
explanation_steps: f = v/λ = 340/2.0 = 170 Hz. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the statement which is not correct regarding charging of a body by friction.
options: An ebonite rod held in one's hand and rubbed vigorously with fur becomes charged.
A glass rod held in one's hand and rubbed vigorously with silk becomes charged.
A metal rod held in one's hand and rubbed vigorously with fur becomes charged.
In charging by friction, charges are transferred from one body to another.
In charging by friction, the charges on the two bodies are equal and opposite.
explanation_steps: A metal rod held in the hand is earthed through the body, so charge does not stay on it.
Insulating rods do become charged. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: The reciprocal of the equivalent of two capacitors in series is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual capacitors.
The charges on two capacitors connected in series depend on the value of the capacitors.
The equivalent capacitance of two capacitors connected in parallel is the sum of the individual capacitances.
The potential difference on two capacitors connected in parallel is the same.
The relation between the charge Q, the potential difference across the capacitor V, and the capacitance C is Q = CV.
explanation_steps: Capacitors in series carry the same charge. The charge does not depend on which capacitor it is.
A, C, D and E are correct. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If the specific gravity of seawater is 1.03, then its density in kg/m³ is
explanation_steps: Specific gravity is density relative to water. ρ = 1.03 × 1000 = 1030 kg/m³. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: When a nucleus emits an alpha-particle, which of the following does not change?
options: The chemical identity of the nucleus.
The total charge of the nucleus plus the emitted alpha-particle.
explanation_steps: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus, so mass number falls by 4, atomic number by 2, and neutron number by 2. The element changes.
Charge is conserved for the nucleus plus the alpha particle. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A cell membrane is 50 angstroms thick. Its thickness in meters and micrometers respectively are
explanation_steps: 1 angstrom = 10⁻¹⁰ m, so 50 angstroms = 5.0×10⁻⁹ m.
1 μm = 10⁻⁶ m, so 5.0×10⁻⁹ m = 5.0×10⁻³ μm. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The dimensions of electrical resistance are
explanation_steps: R = V/I and V = work/charge, so [R] = [energy] / ([charge][current]).
That gives M L² T⁻³ A⁻². Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A machine does 3.6×10⁶ J of work in one hour. Its power in watts is
explanation_steps: Power = work/time = 3.6×10⁶ J / 3600 s = 1000 W. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct about the vectors (2i + 3j) and (i + 2j)?
explanation_steps: Two vectors are parallel only if one is a scalar multiple of the other.
2/1 ≠ 3/2, so they are not parallel. Their cross product is not zero and their dot product is 8, not zero. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A block on a spring has a kinetic energy of 3 J and the spring has an elastic potential energy of 2 J when the block is at x = 2.0 cm. The kinetic energy of the block at x = 0.0 is
explanation_steps: Mechanical energy is conserved on the spring–block system described.
At x = 0 the spring potential energy is zero, so the kinetic energy is 3 J + 2 J = 5 J. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following equations represents motion with constant acceleration?
explanation_steps: Constant acceleration gives a position that is at most quadratic in time.
x = −5t² + 4t has a = −10 m/s². The other equations have changing acceleration or undefined motion. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The muzzle speed of a bullet from a gun is 49 m/s. The maximum horizontal distance at which the bullet can hit is
explanation_steps: Maximum range on level ground is v²/g at 45°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A particle of mass 2 kg moves at 5 m/s in a uniform circular motion of radius 2 m because a cord tied to the particle is anchored at the centre. The power of the force exerted on the particle by the cord is
explanation_steps: The cord force is centripetal, so it is perpendicular to the velocity.
Power = F·v = 0. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A nuclear submarine has a horizontal hull area of 3000 m². The total weight of water on top of the submarine at a depth of 200 m is
explanation_steps: Use the printed sea-water density 1.03×10³ kg/m³ and g = 9.8 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: 0.5 m³ of an ideal gas is heated from 300 K to 500 K at constant volume. The work done on the gas during the heating is
explanation_steps: Work done by an ideal gas is ∫P dV.
The volume is constant, so dV = 0 and the work is zero. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A thin glass plate is exactly 20 cm by 30 cm at 10°C. When its temperature is raised to 40°C, the increase in its area is (α_glass = 9×10⁻⁶ /K)
explanation_steps: Area expansion: ΔA = 2α A ΔT.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which relationship between force F on a particle and its position x implies simple harmonic motion?
explanation_steps: SHM requires a restoring force proportional to displacement, F = −kx.
Only F = −6x has that form. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A car travels at 40 km/h for 2 hours, at 50 km/h for 1 hour and at 20 km/h for 0.5 hour. The average speed of the car (in km/h) is
explanation_steps: Average speed = 140/3.5 = 40 km/h. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A man walks 8 km north and then 6 km in a direction 30° north of east. His resultant displacement (in km) from his starting position is (sin 30° = 0.5, cos 30° = 0.866)
explanation_steps: East component = 6×0.866 = 5.20 km. North component = 8 + 6×0.5 = 11 km.
Resultant = √(5.20² + 11²) = √148.0 = 12.2 km, which is 12 km to the printed precision. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The length of the string of a simple pendulum is 40 cm and the mass of the bob is 0.5 kg. If g = 10 m/s², its angular frequency is
explanation_steps: The bob mass does not enter the angular frequency. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: 7.72 kJ of heat raises the temperature of a 4.0 kg copper block from 300 K to 305 K. The specific heat of copper is
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A coil has resistance 18 Ω at a mean temperature of 20°C and 20 Ω at 50°C. When its resistance is 21 Ω, its mean temperature (in °C) is
explanation_steps: R = R₀(1 + α ΔT). From 18 Ω to 20 Ω over 30 K, α = 2/(18×30) = 1/270 per °C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the INCORRECT statement.
options: The potential difference between two points A and B is the work done in moving a unit test charge from A to B.
The work done in carrying a finite charge between two points at the same potential is zero.
For a uniform field the relation between potential difference V_AB, field E and separation d is V_AB = Ed.
The work done is stored as electric potential energy of the charge.
The unit of potential difference is the volt, defined as V = J·s/A.
explanation_steps: 1 volt = 1 joule per coulomb = 1 J/(A·s), not J·s/A.
A–D match the standard definitions for electrostatic potential. The incorrect statement is E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A cosmic-ray proton reaches the Earth near the equator with a vertical speed of 2.8×10⁷ m/s. The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field there is 30 μT. The ratio of the magnetic force on the proton to its weight is (m_p = 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg, q = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)
explanation_steps: The velocity is perpendicular to the horizontal field, so F_m = qvB.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Two parallel wires in a lamp cord are 2 mm apart. The magnitude of the force per metre between them when each carries 10 A is
explanation_steps: That is 0.01 N/m. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the INCORRECT statement about the magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying wire.
options: Its magnitude is proportional to the current.
Its magnitude decreases as the distance from the wire increases.
It is uniform around the wire.
Its direction is given by the right-hand rule.
explanation_steps: B = μ₀ I /(2π r) is not uniform: it changes with distance and its direction circles the wire.
A, B, D and E are correct. The incorrect statement is C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A closed conducting loop is moved in a uniform magnetic field. The induced emf in the loop
options: depends only on the resistance of the loop.
depends on the shape of the loop.
depends on the magnitude of the magnetic field.
depends on the rate at which the loop is moved.
explanation_steps: Translating a closed loop in a uniform field does not change the flux through it.
The induced emf is therefore zero. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the INCORRECT statement.
options: If the magnetic field through a circuit changes with time, an emf is induced in the circuit.
Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced emf is always opposite to that of the magnetic field which induced it.
For a given rate of change of flux, a coil of many turns has a larger induced emf than a single turn.
If two circuits are close but not touching, a change of current in one can induce an emf in the other.
An isolated circuit carrying a varying current induces a back emf in itself that opposes the change in current.
explanation_steps: Lenz's law says the induced emf opposes the change in flux, not that it is always opposite the inducing field.
A, C, D and E are consistent with Faraday's law and self-induction. The incorrect statement is B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The primary winding of a transformer has 200 turns and the secondary has 50 turns. If the current in the secondary is 40 A, the current in the primary is
explanation_steps: For an ideal transformer, I_p / I_s = N_s / N_p.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The power factor in an a.c. circuit in which X_L = X_C
explanation_steps: When X_L = X_C the circuit is resonant and the phase angle is zero.
The power factor cos φ is 1. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A wave of amplitude A interferes with another wave of the same kind whose frequency is different but whose amplitude is also A. The resulting wave has an amplitude
explanation_steps: Two equal-amplitude waves of different frequency produce beats.
The resultant amplitude varies between 0 and 2A. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Waves of length 5 m pass an anchored boat 1.25 s apart. The speed of the waves is
options: Impossible to tell from the information given.
explanation_steps: The time between successive crests is the period, T = 1.25 s.
v = λ/T = 5/1.25 = 4 m/s. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A force of 50 N is applied to the input piston of a hydraulic system. The input area is 60 cm² and the output area is 15 cm². The force the output piston exerts is
explanation_steps: Pressure is transmitted, so F_out / F_in = A_out / A_in.
F_out = 50 × 15/60 = 12.5 N. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A horizontal pipe of 10 cm² cross-section joins a pipe of 50 cm². The speed in the smaller pipe is 6 m/s and the pressure there is 200 kPa. The speed and pressure in the larger pipe are
explanation_steps: Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ gives v₂ = 6 × 10/50 = 1.2 m/s.
Bernoulli: P₂ = 200 kPa + ½ρ(v₁² − v₂²) = 200 + 0.5×1000×(36 − 1.44)/1000 kPa = 217.3 kPa. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The following forces act on an object: 10 N north, 20 N southeast and 5 N west. The magnitude of their resultant is (sin 45° = cos 45° = 0.707)
explanation_steps: Take east and north as positive. Southeast contributes 14.14 N east and −14.14 N north.
Resultant = √(9.14² + 4.14²) = 10.0 N. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A cannon fires a shell at 1.7 km/s at 55° to the horizontal. The range and time of flight are (sin 55° = 0.819, cos 55° = 0.574, g = 9.8 m/s²)
explanation_steps: Time of flight = 2 v sin 55° / g = 2×1700×0.819/9.8 = 284 s. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A skater has moment of inertia 3.0 kg·m² with arms outstretched and 1.0 kg·m² with arms at her sides. She spins at 1.0 rev/s with arms out, then pulls her arms in. Her final angular speed and the work she has done are
explanation_steps: Angular momentum is conserved, so ω_f = 3.0 × 1.0 = 3.0 rev/s.
Work done = ΔKE = 118 J. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the INCORRECT answer. When an atom decays by emission of a β particle
options: the mass number of the daughter nucleus remains the same.
the mass of the daughter nucleus is approximately equal to that of the parent nucleus.
the atomic number of the daughter nucleus decreases by 1.
the daughter nucleus occupies a different position in the periodic table.
charge is conserved in a β decay.
explanation_steps: β⁻ emission raises the atomic number by 1; it does not decrease it.
Mass number is unchanged, charge is conserved, and the daughter is a different element. The incorrect statement is C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a unit of force?
explanation_steps: Newton, kg·m·s⁻², g·cm·s⁻² (the dyne) and J/m are all force units.
W·m·s = J·m = N·m², which is not a force. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: All of the following quantities are derived quantities except
explanation_steps: Speed, density and volume are derived from base units.
Luminous intensity (the candela) is an SI base quantity. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The volume of an aluminium body X is twice the volume of another aluminium body Y. What can you say about the masses of the two bodies?
options: The mass of Y is greater than the mass of X.
The mass of X is greater than the mass of Y.
The mass of X and the mass of Y are equal.
The masses of X and Y are not comparable.
explanation_steps: Both bodies are aluminium, so they have the same density.
Mass = density × volume, and the volume of X is twice the volume of Y, so the mass of X is greater. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A vector has an x-component of 50 units. Find the y-component and the resultant respectively if the resultant makes an angle of 30° with the y-axis. (cos 30° = 0.866, sin 30° = 0.5)
explanation_steps: An angle of 30° with the y-axis means the x-component is R sin 30°.
50 = R × 0.5, so R = 100 units. The y-component is R cos 30° = 86.6 units. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A man walks 40 m due east, then 50 m due north, then 60 m due west. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant. (tan⁻¹ 0.4 = 21.8°)
explanation_steps: Net displacement is 20 m west and 50 m north.
Magnitude = √(20² + 50²) = √2900 = 53.85 m. The direction is tan⁻¹(20/50) = 21.8° west of north. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 60 m/s. One second later, at the same place, another ball is projected upward at 130 m/s. At what time after the second ball is thrown, and at what height, do they meet?
explanation_steps: Take g = 9.8 m/s² and let t be the time after the second throw.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A red ball of mass 2 kg moving at 4 m/s in the positive x-direction makes an elastic head-on collision with a white ball of mass 4 kg moving at 5 m/s in the negative x-direction. The final velocities of the red and white balls are respectively
explanation_steps: For a one-dimensional elastic collision, v1 = (m1−m2)u1/(m1+m2) + 2m2 u2/(m1+m2).
That gives v_red = −8 m/s and v_white = 1 m/s. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The ideal mechanical advantage of a simple machine is always
options: greater than the actual mechanical advantage.
less than the actual mechanical advantage.
equal to the actual mechanical advantage.
dependent on the nature of the simple machine.
sometimes greater than and sometimes less than the actual mechanical advantage.
explanation_steps: Efficiency = AMA/IMA and is less than 1 when friction is present.
Therefore IMA is greater than AMA. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: When light falls on the surface separating two media, which of the following can happen?
options: A portion of the incident light passes into the second medium.
A portion of the incident light is reflected back with an amplified signal.
A portion of the incident light is absorbed by the second medium.
explanation_steps: At an interface, light may be transmitted and absorbed.
Reflection does not amplify the signal, so B is false. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about light?
options: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of refraction.
If rays start from a point and spread in different directions, the beam is called a converging beam.
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun.
Light travels in a straight line when it crosses the interface between two media.
explanation_steps: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun.
The other statements confuse reflection with refraction, a diverging beam with a converging beam, or ignore refraction at an interface. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a ray rule used to find the image formed by a curved mirror?
options: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focus after reflection from a concave mirror.
A ray directed at the centre of curvature is reflected back along itself for a convex mirror.
A ray through the focus of a concave mirror proceeds parallel to the principal axis after reflection.
A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the centre of curvature after reflection from a convex mirror.
None of the above is used.
explanation_steps: A ray parallel to the principal axis of a convex mirror appears to come from the focus, not from the centre of curvature.
The other listed rules are standard mirror constructions. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A glass rod (n = 1.65) in air has its left end ground to a convex hemisphere of radius 4 cm. A point source is 8 cm to the left of the vertex. Where does the image appear?
explanation_steps: Use n2/v − n1/u = (n2−n1)/R with u = −8 cm and R = +4 cm.
1.65/v − 1/(−8) = 0.65/4, so v = 44 cm to the right of the vertex. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The angles of incidence and refraction for a ray passing from a material into air are 45° and 60°. The refractive index of the material is (sin 45° = 0.707, sin 60° = 0.866)
explanation_steps: n sin 45° = 1 × sin 60°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A ray of wavelength 6.0×10⁻⁷ m travels from air into glass of refractive index 1.45 at 40° to the normal. Which statement is not correct?
options: The speed of the ray in the glass is 2.07×10⁸ m/s.
The angle of refraction is less than the angle of incidence.
The wavelength of the ray in the glass is 4.14×10⁻⁷ m.
The frequency of the ray in the glass is 5×10¹⁴ Hz.
The frequency of the ray is 3.45×10¹⁴ Hz.
explanation_steps: Speed, wavelength and frequency in glass are c/n = 2.07×10⁸ m/s, λ/n = 4.14×10⁻⁷ m and c/λ = 5×10¹⁴ Hz. Refraction bends toward the normal.
3.45×10¹⁴ Hz is not the frequency. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which statement is wrong concerning the human eye and a photographic camera?
options: Both have a converging lens forming a real, inverted and diminished image on a screen.
The camera lens has a fixed focal length, but the eye lens can change shape.
The camera image forms on film and the eye image forms on the retina.
A camera diaphragm controls the aperture, while the iris controls the pupil.
explanation_steps: Each of A–D is a standard similarity or difference between the eye and a camera.
None of those statements is wrong. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: What temperature on the Fahrenheit scale is equal to twice the corresponding Celsius temperature?
explanation_steps: Set F = 2C and F = (9/5)C + 32.
2C = (9/5)C + 32 gives C = 160 and F = 320°F. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An iron block 10 cm × 25 cm × 8 cm has a mass of 500 g. It is heated from 10°C to 45°C. The final density, taking the mass as constant and α_iron = 1.1×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, is
explanation_steps: Initial volume is 2000 cm³, so the initial density is 0.25 g/cm³.
Volume expansion changes the volume by about 0.12%, which does not change the density at the printed precision. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A gas has a volume of 1.75 L at 80 cm Hg and 31°C. It is heated to twice that Celsius temperature and expands to 1.89 L. The final pressure is
explanation_steps: Twice the initial Celsius temperature is 62°C = 335 K, and 31°C = 304 K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An ideal gas has a volume of 0.38 m³, a temperature of 34°C and a pressure of 3.0×10⁵ Pa. If the volume stays constant and the pressure becomes 4.0×10⁵ Pa, the temperature is
explanation_steps: At constant volume, T2 = 307 K × (4.0/3.0) = 409.3 K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A 600 g metal block at 120°C is mixed with 300 g of water at 25°C in a 400 g calorimeter of specific heat 424.8 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹. The final temperature is 35°C. The specific heat of the metal, in J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹, is (c_water = 4200 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹)
explanation_steps: Heat gained by water and calorimeter equals heat lost by the metal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is wrong concerning the states of matter?
options: A solid melts at a definite temperature when heat is supplied.
Conversion of a solid directly to a gas is called evaporation.
Temperature, pressure, surface area and a draught affect the rate of evaporation.
Impurities can change the boiling point of a liquid.
explanation_steps: Direct conversion from solid to gas is sublimation, not evaporation.
The other statements are acceptable at this level. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: The electric force law depends on distance in the same way as the gravitational force law.
The force between two point charges is unchanged if a third point charge is brought near them.
The force exerted by the field of a point charge q on another charge q′ is independent of q′.
Lines of force begin on a positive charge and end on a negative charge.
The number of lines of force per unit area is proportional to the electric field.
explanation_steps: The force on q′ is F = q′E, so it depends on q′.
The other statements match the inverse-square law, superposition as stated, and field-line conventions. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An electron starts from rest in a constant electric field of 3×10⁵ N/C. Its speed after 10⁻⁸ s is
explanation_steps: v = at = 5.27×10⁸ m/s. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Capacitors of 5×10⁻⁶ F, 4×10⁻⁶ F and 9×10⁻⁶ F are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance, in μF, and the charge on each capacitor, in μC, when a 9 V battery is connected across them are
explanation_steps: Series capacitors carry the same charge Q = CV = 1.78×9 = 16.0 μC. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A proton and a deuteron (mass twice the proton mass, same charge) move perpendicular to a magnetic field with equal kinetic energy. The deuteron orbit has radius 16.0 cm. The proton orbit radius is
explanation_steps: r = √(2mK)/(qB). Equal charge and kinetic energy give r ∝ √m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A straight wire at the equator lies east–west. Earth’s field there is 3×10⁻⁵ T and the wire’s mass per unit length is 5×10⁻³ kg/m. The current that makes the magnetic force balance the weight is
explanation_steps: At the equator the horizontal field is perpendicular to an east–west wire.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A single-turn square coil, 0.25 m on a side, is perpendicular to a constant magnetic field. An emf of 15 mV is induced when its area decreases at 0.1 m²/s. The field magnitude is
explanation_steps: |ε| = B|dA/dt| for a single turn with the field perpendicular to the plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A spring has force constant 400 N/m. The work done to stretch it 3.0 cm from equilibrium, and the work done to stretch it from x = 2.0 cm to x = 3.0 cm, are
explanation_steps: Work from equilibrium is ½kx² = ½×400×(0.03)² = 0.18 J.
From 2.0 cm to 3.0 cm the work is ½k(0.03² − 0.02²) = 0.10 J. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: In simple harmonic motion the acceleration is always opposite the displacement.
The period of oscillation is independent of the amplitude.
The total mechanical energy is conserved for damped vibrations.
For a given mass, the period of a spring–mass system is inversely proportional to √k.
explanation_steps: Damping removes mechanical energy, so the total mechanical energy is not conserved.
The other statements are standard SHM results. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: At a crosswalk the siren of an approaching car is heard at 510 Hz. After the car passes, the frequency is 430 Hz. The car’s speed is (speed of sound = 343 m/s)
explanation_steps: The ratio of approaching to receding frequency is (v+vo)/(v−vo) = 510/430.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A 600 kg weather balloon is to lift a 4000 kg package. What helium volume is needed? (helium density 0.178 kg/m³, air density 1.29 kg/m³)
explanation_steps: Buoyancy equals the total weight: V(1.29 − 0.178) = 4600.
V = 4.14×10³ m³. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A copper bar is moved to the right with its axis perpendicular to a magnetic field. If the top of the bar becomes positive relative to the bottom, the magnetic field is
options: in the plane of the page, to the left.
in the plane of the page, to the right.
explanation_steps: Positive charges are driven upward, so v × B is upward with v to the right.
That requires B into the page. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A ball thrown vertically upward is caught at the same height after 3.5 s. Its initial velocity and maximum height are (g = 9.8 m/s²)
explanation_steps: Time of flight is 2u/g, so u = 3.5×9.8/2 = 17.2 m/s.
Maximum height is u²/(2g) = 15.0 m. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A student of mass 60 kg stands at the edge of a circular platform of moment of inertia 200 kg·m² and radius 2 m. The angular velocity is 2 rad/s at the edge. When the student is 0.5 m from the centre, the angular velocity is
explanation_steps: Angular momentum is conserved: (200 + 60×2²)×2 = (200 + 60×0.5²)ω.
ω = 880/215 = 4.09 rad/s. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Two stars of masses M and 4M are separated by a distance d. The distance from M to the point where the force on a third mass is zero is
explanation_steps: Between the stars, GMm/r² = G(4M)m/(d−r)².
d−r = 2r, so r = d/3 from M. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: At the surface of Phobos, g is 0.001 times Earth’s g. If you can jump 2 m high on Earth, how high can you jump on Phobos, and how long does it take to reach that height?
explanation_steps: The same takeoff speed gives height inversely proportional to g, so the height is 2000 m.
Takeoff speed is √(2×9.8×2) = 6.26 m/s, and time to the top is v/g_Phobos = 639 s. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The dimension of the volt in base units of length, mass, time and current is
explanation_steps: One volt is one joule per coulomb.
[V] = M L² T⁻² / (A T) = M L² T⁻³ A⁻¹. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A nucleus has 90 protons and 144 neutrons. After emitting two beta particles followed by an alpha particle, it will have
explanation_steps: Each beta emission raises the proton number by 1 and lowers the neutron number by 1, giving 92 protons and 142 neutrons.
An alpha particle then removes 2 protons and 2 neutrons, leaving 90 protons and 140 neutrons. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: In some state of matter the molecules are widely separated and can move almost freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?
explanation_steps: In a gas the intermolecular spacing is large and molecules move freely in all directions.
Solids have fixed positions; liquids are close together and not free in any direction. A fluid is liquid or gas, which is broader than the condition given. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If M, L, and T represent the dimensions of mass, length, and time, respectively, then which one of the following is the dimension of power?
explanation_steps: Power = work / time. Work has dimension ML^{2}T^{-2}.
Dividing by time gives ML^{2}T^{-3}.
On the paper that is option B. A is force, D is energy, E is ML^{2} (no time).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following in SI unit of time is approximately equal to one day? (Give your answer in two significant figures)
explanation_steps: To two significant figures that is 8.6 × 10^{4} s, which is the value the stem asks for. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following physical quantities is a scalar?
explanation_steps: Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force all have direction (vectors).
Distance is magnitude only: a scalar. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: In motion along a straight line, what does the slope in a velocity-time graph represent?
explanation_steps: Slope of a v–t graph is Δv/Δt, which is acceleration. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: In a uniformly accelerated motion, which one of the following gives the correct relation between velocity and time?
options: Velocity is a quadratic function of time.
Velocity is inversely proportional to time.
Velocity is a cubic function of time.
Velocity is a linear function of time.
explanation_steps: v = u + at is linear in t when a is constant. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A freely falling object is dropped from a height of 20 m. What is the speed (in m/s) of the object when it just hits the ground?
explanation_steps: Dropped: u = 0. Use v^{2} = u^{2} + 2gh with g = 10 m/s^{2}.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In a uniform circular motion of a particle its acceleration is directed toward the center of the circle.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its speed is constant.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its velocity is not constant.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its acceleration is constant.
In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its velocity is perpendicular to its acceleration.
explanation_steps: Centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude v^{2}/r but its direction always points to the centre, so the acceleration vector is not constant.
A, B, C and E are true of UCM. The incorrect statement is D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A motorcar having a mass of 1,000 kg accelerates from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the net force (in newtons) acting on the car?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Normal force acts on the object ______ to the surface.
explanation_steps: By definition the normal force is perpendicular (normal) to the contact surface. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An athlete of 80 kg mass climbs up to a height of 5 m with constant velocity. What is the work (in joules) done by the athlete in lifting his body?
explanation_steps: At constant velocity the net force is zero, but the work done by the athlete against gravity is mgh.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An object, initially at rest, explodes and splits up into two parts. How do the two parts move?
options: One part remains at rest and the other is moving.
At an angle of 45° to each other.
explanation_steps: Initial momentum is zero. Conservation of momentum requires the two fragments to have equal and opposite momenta, so they move in opposite directions. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A force of 10 N acts on a 1 kg block placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The force acts on the block at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. Which one of the following gives the horizontal acceleration of the block in m/s²?
explanation_steps: Horizontal component F_x = 10 cos 60° = 10 × 1/2 = 5 N.
a_x = F_x / m = 5 / 1 = 5.0 m/s^{2}. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is incorrect for an image formed by a plane mirror?
options: The image is the same in size as the object.
The image and object distances from the mirror are equal.
The left hand of the object appears as right hand in the image.
explanation_steps: A plane mirror produces a virtual, laterally inverted image of the same size with |u| = |v|. It is not magnified. The incorrect statement is B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If a ray of light is incident on a smooth surface at an angle of 40°, then what is the angle (in degrees) between the surface and the reflected ray?
explanation_steps: Angle of incidence is measured from the normal. Angle with the surface is 90° − 40° = 50°.
The reflected ray makes the same 50° angle with the surface. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If a ray of light goes from air to a medium of refractive index greater than one, then what will be the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence?
options: Larger than the angle of incidence.
Less than the angle of incidence.
Equal to the angle of incidence.
Not related to the angle of incidence.
Larger or equal to the angle of incidence.
explanation_steps: n_air ≈ 1 < n_medium, so the ray bends toward the normal: r < i. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A spherical concave mirror with an object at its center of curvature produces
options: A virtual image behind the mirror at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
A virtual image in front of the mirror at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
A real, upright, magnified image at an image distance equal to half of the radius of curvature (R).
A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to half of the radius of curvature (R).
explanation_steps: For a concave mirror, object at C (u = R = 2f) gives a real inverted image also at C, same size. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the dimension of the gravitational constant in the units of the SI system?
explanation_steps: From F = G m1 m2 / r^{2}, G = F r^{2} / (m1 m2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A solid object is transferred from the Earth to the Moon. Which one of the following physical quantities of the object is changed?
explanation_steps: Mass, volume and density of a solid are independent of g. Weight W = mg changes because g_Moon ≠ g_Earth. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Two charges, q1 and q2, interact with each other. If the sign of the charge q2 is changed to the opposite, but its magnitude remains the same, what can be said of the force acting on q1 due to q2?
options: The force changes its direction to the opposite only.
The magnitude of the force is increased twice with no change of its direction.
The magnitude of the force is decreased twice and its direction changes to the opposite.
The magnitude of the force is decreased twice with no change of its direction.
explanation_steps: Coulomb force magnitude k|q1 q2|/r^{2} is unchanged if only the sign of q2 flips.
The force reverses (attraction ↔ repulsion). Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Charged particles are moving from terminal A to terminal B in a conductor. Suppose that the magnitude of velocity of each moving charge is doubled. Which one of the following is correct regarding the change of current between A and B?
options: The current changes its direction and its magnitude is doubled.
The magnitude of the current is doubled but no change in its direction.
The current changes its direction only.
The magnitude of the current is increased 4 times.
The magnitude of the current is doubled and its direction is changed to the opposite.
explanation_steps: I = nqAv_d. Doubling drift speed doubles I; the charges still travel A to B so the direction is unchanged. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not true about a current carrying conductor placed in the magnetic field?
options: The force on the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field.
The magnitude of the force acting on the current carrying conductor is directly proportional to the current on the conductor.
The force on the conductor is proportional to the length of the conductor.
The direction of the force changes to the opposite direction with the change of the current to the opposite direction.
There is no change in the direction of the force when magnetic field changes its direction.
explanation_steps: F = I L × B reverses if B reverses. Statement E is therefore not true. A-D follow from F = ILB sin theta and the right-hand rule.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is wrong about heat and temperature?
options: Temperature is a measure of degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin.
The SI unit of heat is calorie.
Heat flows naturally from a body at high temperature to a body at low temperature.
explanation_steps: The SI unit of heat (energy) is the joule, not the calorie. D is wrong.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An adiabatic process occurs
options: with no heat flow into or out of the system.
explanation_steps: Adiabatic means Q = 0: no heat enters or leaves the system. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid column is:
options: independent on the acceleration due to gravity.
independent on the shape of liquid's container.
independent on the atmospheric pressure on the top the column.
dependent on the area of the container.
explanation_steps: P = P0 + rho g h. This does not depend on the shape or area of the container. It does depend on g, density and P0. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The principle of the operation of a hydraulic jack is based on:
explanation_steps: A hydraulic jack transmits pressure undiminished through a confined liquid: Pascal's principle. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If the frequency of a broadcasting radio station is 3 MHz, then the wavelength (in meters) of the radio station is
explanation_steps: f = 3 MHz = 3 × 10^{6} Hz and c = 3 × 10^{8} m/s (given).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: What physical phenomenon causes nodes to be formed during interference of waves?
explanation_steps: Nodes are points of permanent destructive interference (zero amplitude). Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Depending on the direction of vibration, waves can be classified into transverse and longitudinal. Which one of the following is incorrect about these waves?
options: A transverse wave is a wave in which the vibrations are at right angle to the direction of propagation of the wave.
A longitudinal wave is a wave in which the vibrations are along the direction of propagation of the wave.
Waves on the surface of water are longitudinal.
explanation_steps: Surface water waves are primarily transverse / mixed, not longitudinal. C is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A sound wave with an intensity of 4 W/m² is passing through an area of 2 m². What is the intensity of the same wave (in W/m²) when it passes through an area of 1 cm²?
explanation_steps: Intensity is power per unit area of the wave; it does not change merely because a different patch of area is considered.
The intensity remains 4 W/m^{2}. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: In some state of matter the molecules are oscillating near their points of equilibrium and cannot move freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?
explanation_steps: In a solid, molecules vibrate about fixed equilibrium positions and cannot move freely.
Gases and vapours move freely; liquids can flow. A fluid means liquid or gas. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following has the largest number of significant figures?
explanation_steps: 203, 24.2 and 0.130 each have 3 significant figures; 0.0900 has 3 (leading zeros do not count).
10.00 has 4 significant figures because the trailing zeros after the decimal are significant. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following contains two vector quantities and a scalar quantity?
explanation_steps: Displacement and velocity are vectors; speed is a scalar.
A has one vector; B has three vectors; C and E are all scalars. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the linear motion of an object with constant velocity?
options: Distance from the initial position is a linear function of time.
Velocity is a linear function of time.
Distance from the initial position is a quadratic function of time.
Acceleration is a linear function of time.
explanation_steps: Constant velocity means a = 0 and s = vt, so distance from the start grows linearly with time.
Velocity is constant, not a changing linear function, and acceleration is zero. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A body starts from rest and acquires a velocity of 10 m/s in 5 s. What are the acceleration of the body and the distance traveled by it during this time interval?
explanation_steps: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½×2×25 = 25 m. Use g only where needed; here motion is given by the speed change. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A freely falling object is dropped from a tower and hits the ground with a speed of 20 m/s. What is the height of the tower in m? (Use g = 10 m/s².)
explanation_steps: Dropped: u = 0. v² = u² + 2gh ⇒ 400 = 2×10×h ⇒ h = 20 m. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is tangent to the circle.
The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.
The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is directed toward the center of the circle.
The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is perpendicular to its acceleration.
The acceleration of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.
explanation_steps: Velocity in uniform circular motion is tangential, not toward the centre. The centripetal acceleration points to the centre.
A, B, D and E are true. The incorrect statement is C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A motorcar having a mass of 1000 kg accelerates by a net force of 2000 N from rest. What is the speed of the car after 10 seconds (in m/s)?
explanation_steps: From rest, v = at = 2×10 = 20 m/s. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Car A is traveling at 60 km/h due north and another car B is traveling at 70 km/h due south. The velocity of car B relative to A is
explanation_steps: Take north as positive: v_A = +60 km/h, v_B = −70 km/h.
v_B relative to A = v_B − v_A = −130 km/h, that is 130 km/h south. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the wrong statement from the following.
options: The total work done on an object is equal to the change in kinetic energy.
The work done on an object is always positive.
The kinetic energy of a moving object is always positive.
When the speed of an object is doubled its kinetic energy quadruples.
Work and energy have the same units.
explanation_steps: Work can be positive or negative depending on the angle between force and displacement.
A is the work–energy theorem; C, D (KE ∝ v²) and E are true. The wrong statement is B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A particle moving horizontally with a velocity of 10 m/s starts to move up along a frictionless surface (Figure 1). The maximum height h (in meters) the particle will reach is
explanation_steps: On a frictionless rise, ½mv² = mgh, so h = v²/(2g).
h = 10²/(2×10) = 5 m. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg block (initially at rest) placed on a frictionless horizontal surface for 5 seconds (Figure 2). The change in momentum of the block (in kg·m/s) is
explanation_steps: Impulse equals change in momentum: Δp = FΔt = 10×5 = 50 kg·m/s.
The mass is not needed because the force and time are given. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct for an image formed by a plane mirror?
options: The image and the object distances from the mirror are always different.
The left hand of the object appears as the right hand in the image.
explanation_steps: A plane mirror gives a virtual, same-size, laterally inverted image with equal object and image distances.
Only E is correct. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: If a ray of light goes obliquely from water to air, then the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence is
options: Larger than the angle of incidence.
Always less than the angle of incidence.
Equal to the angle of incidence.
Not related to the angle of incidence.
Less or equal to the angle of incidence.
explanation_steps: Water has a higher refractive index than air, so an oblique ray bends away from the normal.
Therefore the angle of refraction is larger than the angle of incidence (until the critical angle). Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A spherical convex mirror with an object placed at a distance equal to the radius of curvature (R) from the surface of the mirror produces
options: A virtual image behind the mirror at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
A virtual, diminished image behind the mirror at a distance less than the radius of curvature.
A real, magnified image at a distance equal to half of the radius of curvature.
A virtual, magnified image at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
A real, erect image at a distance equal to half of the radius of curvature.
explanation_steps: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image behind the mirror, with |v| < |f| and f = R/2, so the image distance is less than R.
It does not form a real image for a real object. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Secondary colors are colors formed by the combination of various primary colors. Which of the following gives the correct combination?
explanation_steps: Additive primaries: red + blue = magenta, red + green = yellow, blue + green = cyan.
Only A is the correct combination. Answer: A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following types of forces holds neutrons and protons together in a nucleus?
explanation_steps: The strong nuclear interaction binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus and overcomes proton repulsion.
Gravity is far too weak; the weak interaction governs some decays. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The electrostatic force between two point charges when separated by 10 cm is 1.2 N. What will be the force (in newtons) if they are brought to a separation of 5 cm?
explanation_steps: Coulomb force is proportional to 1/r².
Separation is halved, so the force is multiplied by 4: 1.2×4 = 4.80 N. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A net charge of 30 C passes through a cross-sectional area of a wire in 2.0 minutes. What is the current in the wire (in amperes)?
explanation_steps: I = Q/t. t = 2.0 min = 120 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect about heat transfer?
options: Gases are poor conductors of heat.
Metals are good conductors of heat.
Transfer of heat by convection occurs only in fluids.
Heat is transferred from the Sun to the Earth mainly by radiation.
Conduction takes place by mass movement of heated particles.
explanation_steps: Conduction transfers energy by particle collisions, not by bulk mass movement. Mass movement is convection.
A–D are accepted statements. The incorrect one is E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct about an isothermal process?
options: It occurs with no heat flow into or out of the system.
It occurs at constant pressure and temperature.
explanation_steps: Isothermal means constant temperature.
Constant pressure is isobaric, constant volume isochoric, and no heat flow is adiabatic. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A heat engine is a device that changes thermal energy into mechanical work.
A temperature difference is required to run a heat engine.
A refrigerator takes heat from a high temperature area and releases it to a low temperature area.
Heat does not flow spontaneously from a cold object to a hot object.
Heat flows naturally from a hot object to a cold object.
explanation_steps: A refrigerator removes heat from the cold region and rejects it to the hotter surroundings, using work.
C reverses that direction, so it is incorrect. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Pressure is the product of force and area.
A pressure of 1 atmosphere is equivalent to 1 newton per square meter.
The standard atmospheric pressure is roughly 760 mm Hg.
A manometer is a device used for measuring atmospheric pressure.
Atmospheric pressure increases as altitude increases.
explanation_steps: Standard atmospheric pressure is about 760 mm Hg (1.01×10⁵ Pa).
Pressure is force per area, 1 atm is not 1 Pa, a barometer measures atmospheric pressure, and pressure falls with altitude. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which statement is not true about absolute pressure at a depth h in an open liquid column?
options: The absolute pressure depends on the acceleration due to gravity.
The absolute pressure depends on the liquid’s density.
The absolute pressure is independent of the shape of the liquid’s container.
The absolute pressure is independent of the atmospheric pressure on top of the column.
The absolute pressure is independent of the area of the container.
explanation_steps: Absolute pressure is P = P_atm + ρgh, so it depends on atmospheric pressure.
D is therefore not true. A, B, C and E follow from that relation. Answer: D.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: A body sinks in a liquid if its weight is more than the weight of the displaced liquid.
A body rises in a liquid if its weight is less than the weight of the displaced liquid.
A body sinks in a liquid if the buoyant force is more than the weight of the body.
A body floats in a liquid if its weight is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid.
The apparent weight of a body floating in a liquid is zero.
explanation_steps: A body sinks when its weight exceeds the buoyant force (weight of displaced liquid), not when buoyancy is larger.
If buoyancy exceeds weight the body rises. C is incorrect. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A sound wave is passing through a tube where the area of the cross-section is 2 cm² and the intensity of the wave is 4 W/m². What is the area (in cm²) of the cross-section of the tube in that place where the intensity of the same wave is 0.5 W/m²? Assume that there are no energy losses.
explanation_steps: With no energy loss, power P = IA is constant, so A₂ = A₁ I₁/I₂.
A₂ = 2 × (4/0.5) = 16 cm². Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The speed of a sound wave is 330 m/s and the wavelength is 330 cm. What is the period of the sound wave in milliseconds?
explanation_steps: T = 1/f = 0.01 s = 10 ms. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about waves?
options: In a transverse wave, particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of motion of the wave.
Mechanical waves do not propagate through vacuum.
Sound wave is a transverse wave.
The speed of electromagnetic waves is much greater than that of mechanical waves.
Waves can carry energy from one place to another.
explanation_steps: Sound in air is a longitudinal wave: particles oscillate along the direction of travel.
C is incorrect. A, B, D and E are true. Answer: C.

questions.prompt: A man standing in front of a high wall hears the echo of his voice after 2 s. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s, his distance to the wall in meters is
explanation_steps: The echo travels to the wall and back, so 2d = vt = 330×2 = 660 m.
d = 330 m. Answer: B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The device which measures the distance to an object by measuring the time required for a radio wave to reach the object and return is called
explanation_steps: Radar uses radio waves and the round-trip time.
Sonar and ultrasonic scanners use sound; a laser uses light. Answer: C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is correct about electromagnetic waves?
options: All electromagnetic waves are affected by electric and magnetic fields.
All electromagnetic waves propagate as uniform electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other.
All electromagnetic waves cannot be polarized.
All electromagnetic waves propagate through vacuum with speeds proportional to their wavelengths.
Electromagnetic waves can show interference and diffraction.
explanation_steps: Electromagnetic waves are transverse waves and show interference and diffraction.
They are oscillating, not uniform, fields; they can be polarized; and in vacuum they all travel at c, not at a speed proportional to wavelength. Answer: E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Line spectra
options: cannot be used to identify elements.
can be produced by low-density monatomic gases and vapour.
can be produced by high-density monatomic gases and vapour.
can be produced by high-density diatomic gases and vapour.
can be produced by high-density polyatomic gases and vapour.
explanation_steps: A hot low-density monatomic gas emits a line spectrum characteristic of the element.
High-density sources tend to give continuous or broadened spectra. Line spectra are used to identify elements, so A is false. Answer: B.
